issues.description: The authors state that the reliabilities for the SDO and RWA scales were 'poorer than is typically the case' but fail to report the actual reliability coefficients (e.g., Cronbach's alpha or McDonald's omega) anywhere in the text or tables.
issues.quote: Reliabilities for SDO and RWA were poorer than is typically the case when the full scales are used, but are consistent with expectations based on previous research using short measures [31].

issues.description: The study uses a 5-year longitudinal design with an initial sample of 22,974 participants, but completely fails to report the attrition rate across the five waves or the proportion of missing data. This is critical for evaluating the validity of the FIML imputation and the representativeness of the final sample.
issues.quote: This study uses data from individuals who participated in the first five years of the project (from 2009 to 2013). Of the 22,974 participants included in this study...

issues.subcategory: Unjustified causal claims from observational data
issues.description: The authors repeatedly use strong causal language based on a cross-lagged panel model of observational data. CLPMs cannot establish causality because they do not account for unmeasured time-varying confounds.
issues.quote: We used cross-lagged path analysis to infer causal associations between SDO, RWA and willingness to sacrifice for the environment.

issues.description: The authors conclude that their findings explain the 'motivation to exploit the environment,' but their actual dependent measure assesses 'willingness to make sacrifices for the environment' (e.g., driving less, paying more). A lack of willingness to sacrifice is conceptually distinct from an active motivation to exploit.
issues.quote: These findings suggest that the motivation to exploit the environment comes primarily from the desire for dominance...

issues.subcategory: Unclear handling of missing indicator in latent model
issues.description: One RWA item was not assessed at Time 2. The authors state they constrained factor loadings to equality across all time points to establish measurement invariance. It is unclear how they handled this missing item in the invariance constraints, and measuring a latent variable with different items across waves threatens longitudinal measurement invariance.
issues.quote: The item “Some of the best people in our country are those who are challenging our government, criticizing religion, and ignoring the “normal way” things are supposed to be done”, was not assessed at time two, but included in all other time points.

issues.description: The authors adopted a 'conservative' p < .01 threshold post-hoc due to the large sample size. While adjusting alpha for large samples can be reasonable, doing so arbitrarily without pre-registration introduces researcher degrees of freedom.
issues.quote: Because of the large sample size of this dataset, we adopted a conservative p-value threshold of p < .01 to indicate significance of findings

issues.description: The authors report a CFI of .86, which is well below standard acceptable thresholds (typically >.90 or >.95). They dismiss this poor fit by incorrectly claiming CFI is negatively affected by model complexity (CFI actually includes a penalty for complexity). Accepting a poorly fitting model undermines the validity of all parameter estimates.
issues.quote: Overall, model fit was poorer for those indices affected by model complexity (e.g. χ2(2279) = 36511.73, p < .001, CFI = .86), however those less influenced by complexity pointed to good fit... therefore the model was accepted.

issues.description: The authors report chi-square difference tests using '2(1)' instead of 'χ2(1)'. This typographical error obscures the statistical reporting.
issues.quote: We found that our original model provides significantly better fit to the data 2(1) = 50.98, p < .001

issues.description: The authors report a chi-square difference of 15,389.13 for the comparison of two lagged effects (B = .02 vs B = -.001). Given the standard errors reported, a chi-square value of this magnitude is mathematically impossible and represents a severe calculation or reporting error.
issues.quote: These lagged effects were also statistically different (2(1) = 15,389.13, p < .001)

issues.description: The authors compare the strength of the unstandardized lagged effect of SDO on WILL to the effect of WILL on SDO to conclude directionality. Comparing unstandardized coefficients across different equations is statistically invalid because the dependent variables have different variances.
issues.quote: However, while the association between SDO and environmentalism was bidirectional, the lagged effect on SDO was stronger than the reverse (2(1) = 39.97, p < .001)

issues.description: The authors constrained all cross-lagged associations to be time-invariant (stationary model) without testing whether this constrained model fits significantly worse than an unconstrained model. This forces the effects to be equal across all 5 years, which may not reflect the actual data.
issues.quote: We imposed this stationary cross-lagged model because we were more interested in the overall and comparative effects of SDO and RWA on changes in environmentalism, and not on whether these effects change during the interval measured.

issues.description: The authors claim their results are 'highly generalisable' because they used a nationally representative sample. However, they fail to acknowledge that non-random attrition over a 5-year longitudinal study typically compromises representativeness.
issues.quote: Our research uses a nationally representative sample, meaning that our results are highly generalisable, at least to the New Zealand population.

issues.description: The authors conclude that New Zealanders are 'socialized into authoritarianism to a greater extent than social dominance' simply because RWA predicts SDO over time but not vice versa. A lagged statistical effect does not directly measure or prove differences in societal socialization processes.
issues.quote: Because we found that RWA predicts SDO over time, but SDO does not predict RWA, this suggests that New Zealander’s are socialized into authoritarianism to a greater extent than social dominance.

issues.subcategory: Failure to disaggregate within- and between-person variance
issues.description: The authors use a traditional cross-lagged panel model, which is known to confound stable between-person differences with within-person changes. Given the very high autoregressive paths (e.g., .95 for RWA), the cross-lagged effects are likely biased by unmodeled trait-like stability. A Random Intercept CLPM (RI-CLPM) should have been used.
issues.quote: The autoregressive cross-lagged panel model allows examination of reciprocal influences among the three variables...

issues.description: The authors mention constraining factor loadings and intercepts to equality to establish measurement invariance, but they do not report the fit of the baseline configural model or the changes in fit indices (e.g., delta CFI) used to justify that scalar invariance was actually achieved.
issues.quote: We started by constraining the factor loadings of our latent variables to equality... Next, we constrained the means (intercepts) of the factors to equality.

issues.description: The model only includes SDO, RWA, and environmentalism, failing to control for basic demographic variables (e.g., age, gender, education, income, political ideology) that are known to correlate with both ideological attitudes and environmentalism. This leaves the model highly vulnerable to omitted variable bias.
issues.quote: The model thus included three latent variables across five measurement points, where each variable within a time point was set to predict each variable in the subsequent time point.

issues.description: The authors suggest their findings highlight endorsers of SDO as targets for climate change communications. Given the very small unstandardized effect sizes (e.g., SDO -> WILL B = -.11 on a 7-point scale), the practical utility of targeting this specific group based on these results is overstated.
issues.quote: Our findings highlight endorsers of SDO as targets for climate change communications.
